subject: Performance follow-up: streaming tail-latency & committed GPU SKU shortlist
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Phil Carroll <phil.carroll@brightmind.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Performance follow-up: streaming tail-latency & committed GPU SKU shortlist

Hi Phil — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and proposed next steps from our side (focused on the SLOs you described):

Summary of BrightMind targets (from today)
- 95th pct tail for streaming (partial tokens) <= 120 ms
- 99th pct tail for streaming <= 300 ms (peak spikes tolerated)
- Sustained throughput target: 9k tokens/s across the pool (mixed prompt lengths)
- Concurrency window: up to 18 concurrent streaming sessions during peak hours

What we validated on the call
- Your workload is heavily streaming (server-side chunking) with ~70% short-turn utterances (~8 tokens) and a 30% long-tail (200+ tokens).
- You need committed capacity with predictable tail-behavior and a fallback path to hosted instances in another region.

Proposed immediate actions (please confirm):
1) We’ll run a focused pilot on a reserved pool with two candidate SKUs: A100-80GB (dense batch-friendly) and H100-80GB (streaming-latency-optimized). I’ve attached a short SKU comparison spreadsheet.
2) We’ll instrument the pilot with a mixed replay of your recent traces (you agreed to share a redacted trace file). Aim: reproduce 95/99 tail and quantify prefix caching gains.
3) Decide commit size: we recommend starting with a 6-card reserved pool (we estimate this meets 9k tokens/s with headroom for spikes) — we’ll provide a sizing calc in 48 hours.
4) Schedule a 90-minute lab run next week (Wed/Fri windows available) to validate tail-latency under controlled cross-traffic.

Attachments: brightmind-demo-notes.pdf (call notes), gpu-sku-comparison-q2.xlsx (SKU quick matrix)

Next steps for you
- Send the sanitized trace (s3 link or attach) and confirm preferred lab windows.
- Any hard constraints on committed SKUs (e.g., procurement block on H100) or approval timelines?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik to finalize the pilot test plan once we have the trace.

Cheers,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Trace: attaching a redacted gzipped event trace (trace_redacted_0626.tar.gz). It contains representative short/long mixes and header timing.
- Procurement: we have budget OK for H100 but procurement prefers a price estimate for each SKU option (including committed discount tiers).
- Windows: Wed 08 Jul or Fri 10 Jul both work for a lab run; prefer morning US-PT.

Two other asks:
1) We need an explicit fall-back behavior: if the reserved pool is saturated can Redwood route to hosted instances with a predictable latency increase and token-cost delta?
2) Can you quantify expected cold-start impact for long sequences (>500 tokens) on both SKUs?

I’ll be out Thu-Fri next week but Phil (ops lead) will attend the run if needed — email phil.ops@brightmind.ai is copied in the trace file link.

—Phil

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Phil Carroll <phil.carroll@brightmind.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance follow-up: streaming tail-latency & committed GPU SKU shortlist

Phil — perfect, thanks for the trace and the procurement note. Quick responses inline: 

- Fallback behavior: yes. We can set routing policy to fail over to hosted instances in a secondary region (us-east) with a well-defined SLO degradation profile. Typical observed behavior in our tests: 95th tail increases by ~1.8–2.5x depending on network egress and model variant. We’ll include the measurable delta in the pilot report.

- Cold-start for long sequences: cold-start (first-token) latency on H100 is materially better for very long sequences because of kernel selection for attention kernels — expect ~15–25% lower first-token times vs A100 under identical batch conditions. However, sustained per-token throughput for batched long sequences is similar once KV caches populate. We’ll quantify this in the lab run and include the per-card tokens/s curve across sequence lengths.

Pilot sizing note: based on the trace, our quick estimate yields:
- H100-80GB (6 cards): ~10k tokens/s steady with 20% safety margin; predicted 95th tail ~90–130ms for short-turn streaming in isolation.
- A100-80GB (6 cards): ~8.2k tokens/s steady; predicted 95th tail ~120–180ms for the same traffic mix.

Action: we’ll put together a test matrix and a per-SKU cost delta table (committed vs on-demand) and share it before EOD. Can Karthik confirm lab window preference (Wed 08 Jul morning PT) and whether we should include an extra mixed-workload spike test?

Thanks — will attach the sizing calc and the rack-level throughput projections in the follow-up.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: sizing_calc_mateo_v1.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Phil Carroll <phil.carroll@brightmind.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance follow-up: streaming tail-latency & committed GPU SKU shortlist

Phil — Karthik here (performance engineering). Wed 08 Jul morning PT works for the lab run. I propose the following test plan outline so BrightMind knows what to expect: 

Lab run outline (90 minutes)
- 15m: baseline run (no cross-traffic) to validate 95/99 tails for short tokens.
- 30m: mixed workload replay (from uploaded trace) to measure steady throughput and tail behavior.
- 15m: injected spike (50% concurrency bump) to validate fallback routing and queuing behavior.
- 20m: long-seq cold-start tests (10 runs at >500 tokens each) to capture first-token and sustained per-token slopes.

Deliverables within 48 hours after the run
- Full lat/throughput report per SKU (csv + graphs)
- A recommended commit (cards, SKU) with cost delta and rollback/fallback playbook
- A short Ops runbook to configure routing and autoscaling thresholds for BrightMind’s control plane

We’ll include run artifacts (logs, Prometheus exports, small benchmark scripts). If procurement needs a sample contract term for an H100 commit, Monica can loop Legal and Sales into the DocuSign draft after the pilot confirms numbers.

Looking forward to the run — please share the sanitized S3 trace link and confirm attendee list for Wed 08 Jul 09:30 PT.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
